record.paper_title: Some Open Problems on Functional Analysis and Function Theory
record.original_question: Describe the separable infinite-dimensional Banach spaces X with the property that whenever another Banach space Y satisfies d(X,Y) = 1, the spaces X and Y are actually isometric.

evidence.quote: Problem 9.2. Describe the separable infinite dimensional Banach spaces X having the following property: for each Banach space Y the condition d(X, Y ) = 1 implies Y ∼= X.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For two isomorphic Banach spaces $X$ and $Y$, the Banach–Mazur distance is defined by
$$d(X,Y)\;=\;\inf\bigl\{\|T\|\cdot\|T^{-1}\|\;:\;T:X\to Y\text{ is a linear isomorphism}\bigr\}.$$
It is well known that $d(X,Y)\ge 1$, with $d(X,Y)=1$ whenever $X$ and $Y$ are isometrically isomorphic; however, in general the converse fails, i.e. there exist non-isometric Banach spaces $X,Y$ with $d(X,Y)=1$.

Give an intrinsic characterization of the separable infinite-dimensional (real) Banach spaces $X$ with the following rigidity property: for every Banach space $Y$,
$$d(X,Y)=1\quad\Longrightarrow\quad Y\text{ is isometrically isomorphic to }X.$$
artifact.status_search_result: A characterization of separable infinite-dimensional Banach spaces $X$ for which $d(X,Y)=1$ forces $Y\cong X$ isometrically does not appear in the literature. Recent works (e.g., on properties not invariant under Banach–Mazur distance 1, and on $\ell^1$-preduals with $d(c_0,\cdot)=1$) continue to exhibit new non-isometric pairs at distance one, indicating the classification problem remains open.

status_evidence.title: On Banach space properties that are not invariant under the Banach–Mazur distance 1
status_evidence.snippet: Studies properties of Banach spaces that fail to be preserved under Banach–Mazur distance equal to 1, demonstrating that distance 1 does not in general imply isometry.
status_evidence.claim: Distance 1 does not imply isometric isomorphism in general, so the characterization problem is nontrivial.

status_evidence.title: A note on the Banach–Mazur distances between c0 and other ℓ1-preduals
status_evidence.snippet: Examines ℓ1-preduals Y with d(c0, Y)=1 that are not isometric to c0.
status_evidence.claim: Examples of non-isometric pairs at Banach–Mazur distance 1 continue to be constructed, with no general characterization.
